analysis.title: "Not Spectacular Enough": Novogratz Says AI Is The Biggest Bubble Of Our Lifetime... And You Should Buy It
key_insights: Mike Novogratz (Galaxy Digital) called AI the biggest bubble of our lifetime at the Greenwich Economic Forum but told investors to buy anyway. His case is that AI-linked stocks still look cheap on price-to-earnings and that bubbles end more spectacularly than this.
Novogratz sees no political brake on AI. He says both US parties view the AI race with China as somewhat existential, so Washington will struggle to slow AI down.
The author notes Novogratz made a similar call on crypto in November 2017 while staying bullish. Bitcoin peaked the following month and fell more than 80%, and Galaxy lost $273 million in 2018.

Ray Dalio called AI a classic bubble that is close to bursting, citing rising interest rates and the need to convert paper wealth into cash. Long-dated Treasury yields are at their highest since 2002.
Dalio warned that China and Japan may pull back from US Treasuries, and said AI firms that used to raise capital through equity now have to shift to debt.

Nassim Taleb agreed with Dalio's diagnosis but named the bond market as the weak point. He worries more about domestic retirees and funds stepping away from long-duration debt than about Beijing or Tokyo.

Taleb called buying AI companies just because the technology is transformative a trap, since historically the companies that benefited were not the pioneers. He recommended always holding a tail hedge.

Goldman's Bobby Molavi reviewed capex booms from railways in 1845 through shale in 2014 and found the usual trigger is a central bank pivot. The sequence is stocks peak, capex keeps rising for 6 to 24 months, then capex rolls, then stocks roll.

Molavi has the AI big 10 at 42% of S&P market cap, above the 1999 TMT peak of 41%. Only the 1830s railroads (63%) and Japan in 1985 (44%) were higher. Market breadth is at its narrowest since the dotcom peak.

Goldman's Tony Pasquariello made a valuation argument closer to Novogratz's. The forward P/E of the median AI infrastructure stock fell from 32x in April to 22x, and the market is more sober about these stocks than in 1999, 2007 or 2021.
AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive half of S&P Q3 earnings growth, with NVDA and MU alone driving a third of it.
The author argues cheap P/E is undercut because earnings increasingly fund capex. The free cash flow yield of the 10 largest stocks is the lowest since the dotcom bubble.
AI-related investment grade bonds trade a record 50bps wide of the rest of IG and increasingly like junk. The author says this debt is drawing demand away from Treasuries.
The author says the central bank pivot has already arrived. The market prices one more Fed hike this year and about two more next year, and long-end yields are at 24-year highs.
Goldman's Monetary Policy Optimism component of its Risk Appetite Indicator fell to -7.98, near the all-time low of -9.38, while the S&P sits at a record.
Bank of America sees a tech bubble brewing and advises clients to buy anyway, hedging with equity derivatives. DBS CIO Hou Wey Fook argues Nvidia at a mid-teens forward multiple cannot be a bubble.
The author's conclusion is that the more likely outcome is a quiet peak in stocks while capex keeps rising, with the spectacular part visible only in hindsight.

sector_views.rationale: Views split. Novogratz, Pasquariello, Bank of America and DBS favor owning AI on valuation. Dalio, Taleb, Molavi and Hartnett warn on concentration, debt funding and rates.

earnings_insights: Goldman's Pasquariello says AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive half of S&P Q3 earnings growth, with NVDA and MU alone driving a third of it (forward-looking expectation, not reported results).
Forward P/E of the median AI infrastructure stock fell from 32x in April to 22x per Pasquariello, who says these companies are delivering. DBS says Nvidia trades in the mid-teens on forward earnings.
The article argues earnings increasingly have to fund capex, and the free cash flow yield of the 10 largest stocks is the lowest since the dotcom bubble.

crypto_views: Novogratz called crypto the biggest bubble of our lifetimes in November 2017 while staying bullish. Bitcoin peaked the next month and fell more than 80%, and Galaxy lost $273 million in 2018.
The author says Novogratz was eventually proven right on bitcoin, but only after a spectacular crash.

risk_factors: A central bank pivot or further Fed tightening, the historical trigger for capex bubble tops.
Weak demand for long-duration Treasuries from foreign holders (China, Japan) or domestic retirees and funds.
AI companies shifting from equity to debt funding, with AI-related IG bonds trading a record 50bps wide of other IG.
Extreme index concentration (42% of S&P) and narrow breadth.
Low free cash flow yield among the 10 largest stocks as earnings fund capex.
Public backlash against data centers over electricity costs and layoff concerns.
European bank stress linked to selling of French OATs.

The author says Japan's selling moved from Treasuries to France's OATs this week, sparking a European doom loop and a plunge in banking stocks.

tension_points.bull_case: Novogratz says AI-linked stocks look cheap on P/E and the bubble is not spectacular enough to end. Pasquariello notes the median AI infrastructure forward P/E fell from 32x to 22x and the market is sober about it.
tension_points.bear_case: Molavi finds capex booms end on a central bank pivot, with stocks peaking before capex rolls, so a top can be quiet. Concentration is at 42% of S&P, breadth is the narrowest since the dotcom peak, and free cash flow yield of the top 10 is the lowest since the dotcom bubble.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A central bank pivot, which Molavi cites as the usual trigger. The article says the market already prices more Fed hikes and long-end yields are at 24-year highs.

tension_points.bull_case: Novogratz sees no political brake on AI spending, and AI investment continues to rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Dalio says rising rates and the need to convert wealth into cash will prick the bubble. Taleb says the bond market is very vulnerable and AI debt competes with Treasuries for the same duration buyers.
